works.title: Angstrom-Precise Vapor-Synthesized Polyamide Membranes for Ion–Ion Separation
works.abstract: Abstract Precise ion–ion separation using nanofiltration (NF) membranes remains a central challenge in water treatment and resource recovery. Conventional fabrication by interfacial polymerization (IP) provides limited control over the structure of the polyamide (PA) selective layer, thereby constraining ion–ion separation. Using a solvent-free, vapor-phase, layer-by-layer approach, we synthesized a PA selective layer for NF via molecular layer deposition (MLD) of trimesoyl chloride (TMC) and piperazine (PIP). This strategy enables angstrom-scale control over PA growth with a deposition rate of 1.3 Å per cycle and yields spatially uniform membranes with a mean pore size of 5.08 Å and a narrow geometric standard deviation of 1.18. MLD further enables precise control over surface chemistry through either TMC or PIP termination. Structural, chemical, and transport characterizations indicate an enhanced size-based exclusion and reduced Donnan exclusion in the MLD-grown membranes. MLD membranes with ∼39 nm-thick PA layer exhibited a water permeance of 13.0 L m–2 h–1 bar–1 and monovalent–divalent cation (Li+/Mg2+) and anion (Cl–/SO42–) selectivities of 36 and 92, respectively. This work establishes MLD-grown PA membranes as a model platform for precise PA structural control and mechanistic interrogation of ion–ion separation, providing design principles for more selective membranes.

works.title: Oxygen Plasma-Activated PES Ultrafiltration Substrates for Constructing High-Performance Mg2+/Li + Separation Nanofiltration Membranes
works.abstract: Abstract Positively charged polyamide (PA) nanofiltration (NF) membranes hold great potential for Mg2+/Li+ separation, but their performance is strongly affected by the surface properties and pore structures of the substrate. In this study, a PES ultrafiltration substrate was pretreated by ethanol natural evaporation and then activated by oxygen plasma prior to interfacial polymerization to fabricate composite NF membranes. The pretreatment effectively suppressed irreversible pore shrinkage of the PES substrate during drying, enabling the E-PES-UF substrate to maintain a high water flux of 228 LMH. Subsequent oxygen plasma activation improved the hydrophilicity and interfacial wettability of the substrate through mild etching and the introduction of polar oxygen-containing groups, thereby promoting the uniform distribution of PEI aqueous-phase monomers on the activated substrate surface. As a result, the optimized E-30-20-NF membrane exhibited a uniform PA layer with a thickness of only 37 nm and an isoelectric point of pH 8.85. It achieved a Mg2+ rejection of 99.3%, a separation factor of 52.8, and a permeation flux of 21.1 LMH. During the 120 h continuous-filtration test, the Mg2+ rejection remained above 98.9%, while the Mg2+/Li+ mass ratio in the permeate was maintained at 0.28–0.40. The membrane also exhibited a good antifouling performance.

works.title: Dual-Regulation of Interfacial Polymerization via Interlayer and Surfactant: Molecular Dynamics Insights and High-Performance Mg2+/Li+ Separation Nanofiltration Membrane
institutions: Institute of New Functional Materials of Guangxi Institute of Industrial Technology , ,
works.abstract: Abstract A polyamide nanofiltration (NF) membrane with high permeance and Mg2+/Li+ selectivity was developed through a dual regulation strategy combining a tannic acid (TA) and Al3+ coordination interlayer with sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS). Molecular dynamics simulations showed that surfactant structure significantly affects the interaction and molecular mobility of polyethylenimine (PEI), with SDS providing effective regulation of PEI transport behavior. The TA and Al3+ coordination interlayer regulates PEI retention and local supply near the substrate surface, while SDS modulates PEI molecular mobility, providing complementary regulation of interfacial polymerization. Structural characterization showed that the dual regulation strategy promoted the formation of a thin and hydrophilic polyamide selective layer and decreased the proportion of surface carboxyl groups from 23.51% for the pristine PA membrane to 13.36% for the TA-Al3+/PA-SDS membrane, resulting in favorable surface charge characteristics. The optimized membrane exhibited a MgCl2 rejection of 99.26%, a LiCl rejection of 32.9%, an Mg2+/Li+ separation factor of 44.36, and a water permeance of 10.21 L·m−2·h−1·bar−1. The membrane also maintained relatively stable separation performance during 72 h filtration. These results demonstrate that coordinated regulation of PEI supply and molecular mobility provides an effective strategy for constructing high performance NF membranes for Mg2+/Li+ separation and lithium recovery from brines.

works.title: Ordered MoS2 Nanochannels Regulated by CNT for Conformation-Dependent Sieving in High-Salinity Organic Wastewater
works.abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of the pharmaceutical and fine chemical industries has escalated the discharge of high-salinity organic wastewater, which contains complex solutes and biotoxic antibiotics that are difficult to treat conventionally due to their high osmotic pressure and environmental persistence. Here, we developed a high-performance composite nanofiltration membrane by incorporating hydroxylated single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNT-OH) into electrochemically exfoliated monolayer MoS2 nanosheets. SWCNT-OH acts as a structural regulator, preventing MoS2 restacking and constructing stable, highly ordered 1.5 nm interlayer channels. At an optimized mass ratio of 6:1, the membrane achieves a water permeance of 28.0 L·m–2·h–1·bar–1 and a separation factor of 59.8 for oxytetracycline (OTC)/NaCl mixtures. Notably, rejection is governed by the molecular projected cross-sectional dimension relative to the 1.5 nm channels, demonstrating a conformation-dependent selectivity. These results highlight MoS2/CNT membranes as a durable solution for sustainable industrial wastewater treatment.

works.title: Graphene Oxide (GO)/Polyamide Thin-Film Nanocomposite Membranes for Enhanced Pervaporation Desalination: Role of GO in Microstructural Modification and Water Transport
institutions: Department of Chemical Engineering, Jieyang Polytechnic, Jieyang 522000, China
MayAir Technology (China) Co., Ltd., Nanjing 210000, China
State Key Laboratory of Radio Frequency Heterogeneous Integration, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen 518060, China
Institute for Advanced Study, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen 518060, China
College of Civil and Transportation Engineering, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen 518060, China
works.abstract: Pervaporation (PV) desalination offers a viable route for high-salinity wastewater treatment, yet its broader implementation is constrained by limited membrane permeability. In this study, graphene oxide (GO)/polyamide (PA) thin-film nanocomposite (TFN) membranes were prepared through interfacial polymerization, wherein GO nanosheets were pre-dispersed in the aqueous m-phenylenediamine phase at different loadings. The prepared membranes underwent comprehensive characterization to evaluate the effects of GO incorporation on surface compositions and properties. Complementary molecular dynamics simulations were employed to explore the molecular-scale water diffusion within the membrane matrix. The results demonstrated that GO effectively enhanced the surface hydrophilicity, reduced the selective layer thickness, rendered the water–membrane binding energy more negative, and increased the fractional free volume, collectively boosting the pervaporation flux. The optimal membrane delivered a flux of 22.38 L m−2 h−1, surpassing the pristine PA membrane by 31%, while maintaining a salt rejection of 99.9% at 70 °C using a 3.5 wt% NaCl feed solution. It also exhibited stable performance at higher salinities, maintaining a flux of 14.4 L m−2 h−1 and rejection above 99.9% at 10 wt% NaCl. This work provides a straightforward protocol for PA-based TFN membranes with enhanced performance in PV desalination, offering molecular-level insights into the role of GO in modifying membrane microstructure and transport properties.

works.title: Lithium Extraction from Dilute Simulated Brines by Membrane-Assisted Liquid-Liquid Extraction Using [P6,6,6,14][PHOS]: Li+/Mg2+ Selectivity in an NF90 Nanofiltration Contactor
institutions: Universidad Católica de la Santísima Concepción
Departamento de Química Ambiental, Facultad de Ciencias, Universidad Católica de la Santísima Concepción, Concepción 4090541, Chile

Grupo en economía circular y tecnologías ambientales, Facultad de Ingeniería y Negocios, Universidad de Las Américas, Santiago 7500975, Chile
Departamento de Ingeniería Química, Facultad de Ingeniería, Universidad de Concepción, Concepción 4070386, Chile
works.abstract: Selective lithium recovery from dilute brines remains challenging because Li+ must be separated from competing ions, particularly Mg2+. In this work, a commercial NF90 nanofiltration membrane was used as a non-dispersive interface between a simulated brine and the hydrophobic ionic liquid [P6,6,6,14][PHOS]. Individual-salt experiments yielded apparent overall mass transfer coefficients of 638 ± 273, 100.5 ± 19.8, and 10.1 ± 0.7 L m−2 h−1 for Na+, Li+, and Mg2+, respectively. Replacing water with 10% (v/v) [P6,6,6,14][PHOS] in hexane as the receiving phase increased Li extraction from 18.6 ± 3.0% to 40.9 ± 2.0%. Under direct Li+/Mg2+ competition, selectivities of 2.19 ± 1.10 and 3.83 ± 0.56 were obtained with the diluted and neat ionic liquid receiving phases, respectively. With neat [P6,6,6,14][PHOS], Li extraction reached 40.3%, and 6.0% of the extracted Li was subsequently recovered in pure water under non-optimized conditions. CHNS analysis showed no detectable transfer of organic material derived from the ionic liquid to the aqueous feed. Overall, NF90 was the main source of Li+/Mg2+ transport discrimination, whereas [P6,6,6,14][PHOS] mainly increased Li uptake.

works.title: Influence of pressure on the separation of L-citrulline from watermelon rind juice by nanofiltration
works.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of extracting L-citrulline from watermelon rind juice using nanofiltration under varying operating pressures from 10 to 40 bar. A nanofiltration membrane DK2540F30 with an active filtration area of 2.6 m² and a fully recirculating feed mode was utilized. The effect of pressure was discovered by monitoring the permeate fluxes of pretreated watermelon rind juice in comparison to that of pure water. Simultaneously, the selective separation of L-citrulline and D-glucose in the permeate was also investigated. The permeate flux of pure water demonstrated a linear correlation with the applied pressure within the range of 10 to 40 bar, whereas the flux behavior of the pretreated watermelon rind juice displayed a non-linear response under the same conditions. The optimal operating pressure was determined to be 35 bar, at which the membrane flux achieved its peak value of 30.00 L.m- ².h - ¹, and a significant rejection rate between L-citrulline (-172.26%) and D-glucose (48.43%) was observed. Membrane fouling was also found at this particular pressure as indicated by a pronounced reduction in permeate flux within the first 5 min, followed by a gradual and sustained decline over time. This reduction was mainly associated with a pronounced rise in fouling resistance, which nearly doubled within the first 9 min and was followed by a gradual increase until the 12-minute mark. A pronounced disparity in rejection rates was observed between Lcitrulline (-172.26%) and D-glucose (48.43%). These findings highlight the capability of nanofiltration as an innovative separation approach for the efficient extraction of Lcitrulline from watermelon rind juice.

works.title: Mechanistic insights into ultrafiltration fouling mitigation by coagulation pretreatment in livestock biogas slurry treatment
institutions: Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography
State Key Laboratory of Desert and Oasis Ecology
works.abstract: The treatment and utilization of livestock biogas slurry (BS) is significantly hindered by severe membrane fouling associated with high turbidity and complex dissolved organic matter (DOM). This study established an integrated coagulation-ultrafiltration (UF) pretreatment system using aluminum sulfate or ferric chloride as coagulants to provide stable influent for subsequent membrane concentration. Results demonstrated that while raw BS caused a rapid increase in transmembrane pressure (TMP) during UF, optimized coagulation at 3 g/L maintained TMP below 10 kPa over 6 h. Specifically, reversible resistance ( R re ) decreased by 92.9–99.0%, and irreversible resistance ( R ir ) decreased by 65.9–79.0%. Particle-related characteristics were closely associated with R re , whereas R ir was governed by multiple interacting factors. Mechanistically, interfacial thermodynamic analysis revealed that optimized coagulation increased the interaction free energies for both membrane-foulant adhesion and foulant-foulant cohesion. This weakened the driving forces for foulant attachment and compaction, resulting in a thinner and looser fouling layer. Nutrient behavior was highly selective during coagulation-UF process. Nitrogen and potassium were largely preserved in the liquid phase, whereas phosphorus exhibited over 99% apparent concentration decrease under the optimized conditions, resulting in an overall nutrient concentration decrease of approximately 12%. Extended 24-h UF and downstream nanofiltration (NF) experiments further supported the improved fouling mitigation benefits of optimized coagulation. These results provided a mechanistic insight and a practical strategy for fouling-controlled BS pretreatment toward subsequent water reuse and nutrient management.

works.title: Techno-Economic Assessment of Membrane Distillation for Green Hydrogen Production in Australia
institutions: Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Monash University, Clayton, VIC 3800, Australia
Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Monash University, Clayton, VIC 3800, Australia
Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Monash University, Clayton, VIC 3800, Australia
Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Monash University, Clayton, VIC 3800, Australia
works.abstract: As global momentum builds toward decarbonisation, green hydrogen has emerged as a key pillar in Australia’s transition to a net-zero emissions future. However, the freshwater demands of large-scale electrolysis poses a significant social hurdle, particularly in a nation facing acute water scarcity. The SeaHydrogen approach, developed in the Netherlands, offers a potential solution by using waste heat from the electrolysis process to desalinate seawater via membrane distillation, enabling hydrogen production without drawing on limited freshwater supplies. This paper investigates the techno-economic feasibility of using membrane distillation as the desalination method for green hydrogen production, when compared to conventional reverse osmosis. The Arrowsmith Hydrogen Project in Western Australia was used as a case study to link the investigation to real world applications. Hydrogen electrolysis requires significant volumes of purified water, posing challenges in water-scarce regions such as regional Australia. Eight scenarios were modelled using brackish aquifer and seawater sources to evaluate capital expenditure, operational expenditure, levelised cost of water, and net present value for both desalination technologies. Results showed that membrane distillation achieved lower levelised cost of water values than reverse osmosis across all configurations (with reductions in cost between 15–37% for the cases considered). This was primarily due to its ability to utilise low-grade waste heat from electrolysers, substantially reducing energy demand and operational expenditure. Aquifer-sourced membrane distillation emerged as the most economically viable configuration. Integrated membrane distillation also presents other potential benefits, including lower energy intensity, reduced-liquid discharge, improved waste-heat recovery, and the option to produce a limited volume of surplus distilled water, either for on-site use or to supplement small local communities. The findings highlight membrane distillation as a promising alternative to reverse osmosis for sustainable hydrogen production, consistently delivering water for lower cost for the Arrowsmith site. Moreover the analysis shows that both methods can be used to generate excess potable water at prices that are competitive with existing water supplies.

works.title: Hydration channel engineering in Tröger’s base-POP membranes for mono/multivalent cation and anion discrimination
institutions: East China University of Science and Technology
works.abstract: Sustainable recovery of critical resources from complex aqueous streams is constrained by membranes that fail to combine rapid ion transport with precise mono/multivalent discrimination. Here, we report Tröger’s base-derived porous organic polymer (POP) membranes with rigid, covalently crosslinked microporous frameworks that stabilize angstrom-scale transport channels while suppressing hydration-induced swelling. These membranes render rapid monovalent-ion transport with near-complete exclusion of multivalent cations and anions, including Mg 2+ , Al 3+ , SO 4 2− , and PO 4 3− . Experiments and simulations show that steric confinement, dehydration penalties, and electrostatic interactions cooperatively raise migration barriers for multivalent ions in confined channels. The membranes achieve comprehensive mono/multivalent discrimination across both cationic and anionic systems. In multistage electrodialysis, they enable stage-amplified lithium enrichment from high-Mg brines with stable long-term operation and downstream recovery of crystalline Li 2 CO 3 . They also facilitate high-purity NaCl enrichment from simulated seawater. Overall, this platform offers a durable and energy-efficient route to selective resource recovery from complex aqueous streams.

works.title: Interfacial Control of Pebax/PDMS-b-PEO Composite Membranes via Air Plasma Treatment for Enhanced CO2/N2 Separation
works.abstract: Pebax selective layers contain hydrophilic polyethylene oxide (PEO) segments. These polar chains do not spread uniformly on hydrophobic polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) intermediate layers. This poor wetting makes defect-free composite membranes difficult to obtain for CO2/N2 separation. Although air plasma (AP) treatment could enhance surface hydrophilicity and promote Pebax adhesion, excessive treatment duration inevitably leads to an over-thickened selective layer and the formation of a dense SiOx barrier, severely compromising gas permeability. To address this trade-off, this study proposes a synergistic strategy combining AP surface engineering with precise blade-gap adjustment to control the Pebax selective layer thickness. PDMS-b-PEO was introduced into the PDMS intermediate layer to mitigate plasma-induced permeability loss through PEO segment migration. Systematic characterization revealed that AP treatment primarily improves Pebax coating through hydrophilic modification rather than etching effects. The optimized membrane, treated with AP for 20 s at a PDMS:PDMS-b-PEO ratio of 1:1, achieved a CO2 permeance of 1711.6 GPU and a CO2/N2 selectivity of 44.4, representing an optimal balance between permeability and selectivity. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further elucidated that the Pebax/PDMS-b-PEO blend network forms “synergistic polar regions,” enhancing CO2 adsorption energy from −20.77 kJ/mol to −26.26 kJ/mol while leaving N2 adsorption unchanged, thereby increasing the CO2/N2 adsorption selectivity by 68.2%. These findings demonstrate that interfacial engineering combined with thickness control offers a facile and effective route for high-performance CO2 separation membranes.

works.title: Silane-modified photothermal membrane with enhanced interfacial evaporation for high-efficiency lithium extraction from salt lake brines
works.abstract: Existing solar-driven interfacial evaporation systems for lithium extraction are limited by insufficient evaporation rates and poor Li + /Na + separation. Here, silane-modified acrylic resin (SMA) is introduced to fabricate carbon nanotube/carbon black composite photothermal membranes (CCS) with enhanced interfacial evaporation. Under 1 sun illumination, the optimized CCS-9 membrane achieves an evaporation rate of 1.73 kg·m −2 ·h −1 , exceeding the theoretical evaporation limit of pure water (1.48 kg·m −2 ·h −1 ). This superior performance originates from synergistic heat management and interfacial water regulation: the thermally insulated substrate limits total heat loss to 6.78%, while surface Si O Si groups tailor the hydrogen-bonding network of interfacial water, increase the fraction of intermediate-state water, and reduce the equivalent evaporation enthalpy to 1918.6 J·g −1 . Integrated into a multistage spatial crystallization evaporator, the CCS-9 membrane delivers a LiCl/NaCl separation factor of 38.5 and a LiCl crystallization rate of 8.7 g·m −2 ·h −1 . Pilot-scale outdoor experiments further demonstrate stable evaporation and ion separation under an average solar irradiance of 0.68 kW·m −2 , while preserving the intrinsic separation mechanism. Thermodynamic analysis confirms the phase transition-driven ion partitioning process, and techno-economic evaluation indicates an equivalent energy consumption of 0.086 kWh·g −1 for LiCl recovery, corresponding to an 18.6% reduction in production cost compared with conventional evaporation ponds. This work provides an effective strategy for high-efficiency solar-driven lithium extraction and promotes the practical application of sustainable brine resource recovery.

works.title: Dual-Layer Architecture in Hollow Fiber Membranes for Enhanced H2, CO2, and SF6 Separation
institutions: North East Institute of Science and Technology
Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research
CSIR-North East Institute of Science and Technology , , , ,
Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research (AcSIR) , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract The growing demand for efficient hydrogen purification and the recovery of high-global-warming-potential gases has intensified the development of compact, energy-efficient membrane processes for industrial gas separation. Composite hollow fiber membranes (HFMs) provide an effective platform for integrating a multilayer structure of a porous substrate and a thin selective layer. However, the applicability of multilayer polymeric HFMs beyond conventional CO2 capture systems remains underexplored, particularly for gas pairs with different molecular sizes. In this study, a dual-layer PES/PDMS/PEBAX-1657 HFM comprising a PES substrate, an ultrathin PDMS gutter layer (∼85 nm), and a PEBAX-1657 selective layer (∼150 nm) was fabricated via sequential coating and investigated for the separation of H2, CO2, N2, and SF6. The performance of the membrane was evaluated using H2, CO2, N2, and SF6 as molecularly distinct probe gases over a pressure range of 1–5 bar. The PES/PDMS/PEBAX-1657 membrane exhibited H2, CO2, N2, and SF6 permeances of 140.82, 71.87, 25.02, and 16.56 GPU, respectively, at 30 °C and 5 bar. This work establishes the PES/PDMS/PEBAX-1657 HFMs as a versatile platform for fundamentally different gas-separation systems, rather than being introduced solely for CO2 capture/hydrogen purification. The combination of high gas permeance and a mechanically robust hollow fiber configuration offers potential for high-throughput operation with reduced membrane-area requirements, while selective-layer and interfacial engineering provide scope for further enhancement of separation selectivity. These findings establish the PES/PDMS/PEBAX-1657 structure as a promising multilayer HFM platform for hydrogen recovery and SF6 separation in electrical power industry applications.

works.title: Polymer-modified MXene thin-film nanocomposite membranes for forward osmosis
works.abstract: Abstract Water scarcity demands novel solutions to address the challenges posed by increasing societal needs. This study presents a novel strategy for fabricating MXene-based thin-film nanocomposite forward osmosis (TFN-FO) membranes with enhanced permeability and selectivity, offering a promising advancement in water treatment technologies. The approach involves synthesizing MXene-functionalized polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP-g-MXene) additives through a facile chemical grafting method, where hydroxyl groups serve as linkers to covalently bond PVP onto the surface of 2D MXene nanosheets. Subsequently, PVP-g-MXene is incorporated into a polyamide (PA) thin film via interfacial polymerization (IP) to produce the innovative TFN-FO membranes. Characterization of MXene and PVP-g-MXene was performed using FT-IR, XRD, TGA, and FE-SEM. The fabricated membranes were analyzed for surface morphology, roughness, and hydrophilicity using FESEM, AFM, and water contact angle (WCA) measurements. The results indicate that incorporating PVP-g-MXene significantly alters the physicochemical properties of the membranes, including morphology, roughness, hydrophilicity, and overall performance during the IP process. All modified membranes demonstrated improved water flux compared to the pristine TFC membrane, with TFN-PgM1 and TFN-PgM2 exhibiting superior selectivity. Notably the representative TFN-PgM2 membrane exhibited a water flux of 18.5 LMH, which is approximately 72% higher than that of the TFC membrane, and demonstrated a Js/Jw ratio of 0.167, indicating an 18.1% improvement in selectivity performance. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of polymer-modified MXene for the development of high-performance FO membranes.

works.title: Water at the Interface: How Membrane Charge Controls Nanoplastic–Lipid Interactions
works.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
works.abstract: Abstract Nanoplastics are pervasive environmental contaminants capable of crossing biological barriers and interacting with cell membranes. However, the molecular mechanisms by which they perturb lipid interfaces remain poorly understood. Here, we combine Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), ultrafast two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy (2D IR), and surface-enhanced infrared absorption (SEIRA) spectroscopy to investigate how anionic polystyrene nanoplastic (NP) particles modulate the environment at the lipid–water interface in model lipid membranes by varying composition and ionic environment. Neutral phosphatidylcholine (POPC) and anionic phosphatidylcholine/phosphatidylserine (POPC/POPS) membranes were used to probe the role of membrane charge on NP-induced interfacial perturbations. FTIR measurements show that NP-induced dehydration of the lipid headgroup region depends strongly on membrane composition, with partial dehydration observed in neutral POPC membranes but negligible changes in anionic POPC/POPS membranes. 2D IR spectra show that NPs induce faster H-bond fluctuations, as water molecules become more labile at the interface. SEIRA measurements further show that these interfacial perturbations are accompanied by localized changes in the acyl-chain ordering. Addition of Ca2+ enhances NP-induced changes to the negatively charged membranes, resulting in hydration dynamics and acyl-chain ordering that resemble those observed in neutral POPC membranes. These results are consistent with the hypothesis that interfacial dehydration is an early event associated with NP-membrane interactions and highlight the role of membrane charge and ionic environment in modulating these interactions.

works.title: Photothermal Evaporator with MXene‐Regulated Fe <sup>3+</sup> /Fe <sup>2+</sup> Cycling via Ligand‐to‐Metal Charge Transfer for Solar Desalination and Wastewater Purification
institutions: School of Textile Science & Engineering Xi′an Polytechnic University Xi′an Shaanxi China
Key Laboratory of Functional Textile Material and Product Ministry of Education (Xi'an Polytechnic University) Xi'an Shaanxi China
Key Laboratory of Functional Clothing Fabric of Shaanxi Province Xi'an Polytechnic University Xi'an Shaanxi China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Combining interfacial solar evaporation and advanced oxidation provides a promising approach to ease global energy shortages and water pollution. However, fabricating bifunctional evaporators with excellent photothermal, catalytic and synergistic properties remains a tough technical challenge. In this work, a glass fiber membrane was adopted as the functional substrate to anchor MXene/MIL‐101(Fe) composites, thereby constructing a bifunctional evaporator (M/T‐GFM) integrating photothermal and catalytic capacities. As a photothermal component, MXene captures solar light and converts light energy into thermal energy to boost peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation. Meanwhile, MXene acts as an electron donor to accelerate the Fe 3+ /Fe 2+ redox cycle within MIL‐101(Fe) via ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT). It takes merely 20 min to degrade high‐concentration Reactive Blue 19 (R.B.19) of 100 mg L −1 completely and 84.32% of phenol in the condensed water, while the water evaporation rate hits 2.49 kg m −2 h −1 . Meanwhile, it exhibits excellent purification on actual dyeing and finishing wastewater. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations clarify PMS activation over Fe‐O‐Ti and Fe‐O sites. Relying on the synergistic mechanism where MXene‐mediated photothermal conversion and LMCT accelerate the Fe 3+ /Fe 2+ redox cycle, this study provides a new strategy for concurrent freshwater generation and wastewater remediation combining interfacial evaporation and a PMS based advanced oxidation process.

works.title: Toward Low-Carbon Seawater Desalination: Integrating Thermal and Membrane Technologies, Renewable Energy, and AI Optimization with Life-Cycle Assessment
institutions: Department of Civil Engineering, University of Alaska Anchorage, Anchorage, AK 99508, USA

works.abstract: Seawater desalination can only be sustainable if it cuts energy use, membrane fouling, brine discharge, and water cost. This review compares thermal and membrane technologies against these four challenges. RO supplies 70 to 80% of desalinated water at 3 to 5.5 kWh/m3, against 6.5 to 12 for MED and vapor compression and 13.5 to 25.5 for MSF, and it usually gives the lowest water cost, though energy prices and brine rules shift this. Thermal processes still yield purer distillate. A life-cycle appraisal structured by ISO 14040 and 14044 finds that energy drives most RO emissions, that brine recovery lowers impacts, and that low-carbon heat or different criteria weights can reverse technology rankings. Hybrids target recovery and scaling: RO–MSF and NF–RO have commercial or pilot cases, whereas MSF–MED and MD-based options rest on simulations and pilot work. AI models now optimize energy use, forecast fouling, and monitor water quality, but rarely link thermal, brine, and life-cycle stages. Priorities are fouling-resistant membranes, renewable-powered hybrids, brine minimization, and joint AI and life-cycle assessment.

works.title: Preparation of Membrane Evaporators and Solar Interfacial Water Evaporation Performance Study
institutions: China University of Petroleum, East China
works.abstract: Abstract Membrane evaporators are widely used in solar interfacial water evaporation due to their low cost and convenient construction. However, they generally suffer from issues such as low evaporation rate, poor light absorption and temperature rise capacity, and weak salt resistance during evaporation in seawater. To address these issues, this study conducted ultrasonic treatment on membranes from medical absorbent cotton (AC) using ethanol as the medium for the evaporator. The membranes were coated with C and Fe elements using the impregnation metho and enriched with Ti elements using the in situ growth method. Then, the evaporators containing different elements were tested for photothermal water evaporation, surface temperature rise capacity under illumination, and salt resistance for seawater desalination. The results showed that different elements affect the weight loss curve, evaporation rate, and evaporation efficiency of the samples. The addition of Fe element on the basis of a C element coating can optimize the evaporation capacity of the sample, achieving an evaporation rate of 1.44 kg·m–2 under simulated 1 sun pure water conditions. The incorporation of Ti element effectively enhances the salt resistance of the membrane.

works.title: ADSORPTION PROPERTIES OF Mg-MOF-74: A REVIEW OF LITERATURE DATA AND APPLICATION PROSPECTS
works.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
works.abstract: This review examines published data on gas adsorption in Mg-MOF-74 and the relationship between its structural features and adsorption performance. The roles of open magnesium sites, equilibrium CO2 uptake, gas mixture separation, and the effects of water vapor on active site accessibility are analyzed. Application prospects are shown to depend on the combined effects of selectivity, working capacity, regenerability, and framework stability over repeated adsorption-desorption cycles. Directions for developing effective adsorbents and mixed-matrix membranes for selective carbon dioxide capture are discussed.

works.title: Bioinspired Self-Floating Hydrogel-Coated Foam for Synergistic Solar Power Generation and Desalination
institutions: Shenzhen Polytechnic University , 7098 Liuxian Avenue , Nanshan District, ,
works.abstract: Abstract Interfacial solar-driven evaporation provides a sustainable route for freshwater generation, but practical implementation remains limited by salt accumulation, insufficient understanding of water/ion transport, and inefficient utilization of the evaporated vapor. Herein, we report an interfacially engineered self-floating hydrogel-coated foam evaporator constructed by anchoring Ketjen black/sodium alginate/tannic acid/Fe3+ networks onto a melamine foam skeleton. The Fe3+ ions serve as multivalent coordination centers, simultaneously interacting with the carboxylate groups of sodium alginate and the phenolic groups of tannic acid, thereby forming a stable hydrophilic coating with enhanced surface wettability and robust interfacial adhesion. The open-cell macroporous foam provides low-resistance water supply pathways, while the hydrophilic hydrogel coating promotes surface-mediated water spreading and salt redissolution. Under 1 sun illumination, the optimized evaporator exhibits an evaporation rate of 3.56 kg m–2 h–1 and a solar-to-vapor efficiency of 92.4%. This performance is attributed to broadband solar absorption, localized heat management, and reduced effective evaporation enthalpy of interfacial water. The evaporator maintains stable evaporation in seawater for 120 h without obvious salt crystallization, mainly owing to capillary rewetting, concentration-gradient-driven ion diffusion, and density-driven brine exchange through the macroporous network. In addition, the device enables simultaneous hydrovoltaic electricity generation using inert electrodes. This work provides a chemically and structurally integrated strategy for solar desalination and water-enabled energy harvesting.

works.title: A Columnar Shear-Assisted Freeze Desalination System
institutions: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology , , Clear Water Bay ,
works.abstract: Abstract Freeze desalination is an emerging desalination technique. Previous studies showed that shear-assisted freeze desalination could achieve drinking water production through one freezing cycle. However, the productivity of this approach is relatively low and the energy consumption is relatively high. To address these drawbacks, we developed a columnar shear-assisted freeze desalination system, where seawater flows through a vertical tube with ice formed at the inner surface of the tube. At constant seawater flow rates, potable water is produced at high flow rates. Unfortunately, the drinking water productivity remains low (0.48 kg·m–2·h–1) and the energy consumption is high. By linearly lowering the seawater flow rate during freezing, the drinking water productivity reaches 2.28 kg·m–2·h–1, a 4.8-fold increase compared to the cases with constant flow rates, and the total specific energy consumption is significantly reduced from 11.64 to 1.20 kWh·kg–1. Experiments with natural seawater are also conducted. Due to the relatively low salinity of the natural seawater used (32.53 g·L–1), the productivity of drinking water and the total specific energy consumption reach 5.32 kg·m–2·h–1 and 0.83 kWh·kg–1, respectively. The results indicate that the proposed desalination system is promising for commercialization.

works.title: Microwave-Assisted Degradation of Unsaturated Polyester Resin into HDPE-Modified Aerogels for Oil Adsorption and Oil/Water Separation
institutions: Key Laboratory of Oil & Gas Fine Chemicals, Ministry of Education, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, School of Chemical Engineering, Xinjiang University, Urumqi 830017, China
School of Mechanical Engineering & Center for Post-Doctoral Studies of Mechanical Engineering, Xinjiang University, Urumqi 830017, China
works.abstract: Thermosetting unsaturated polyester resin (UPR) is difficult to reprocess because curing generates an irreversible three-dimensional network. Here, cured UPR was treated in a microwave-assisted hydrazine hydrate/NaOH medium at 70 °C for 30 min to produce a water-swellable UPR-derived product (NUPR). NUPR was combined with glutaraldehyde, subjected to freeze–thaw processing and freeze-drying, and subsequently modified with high-density polyethylene (HDPE) to fabricate porous aerogels. FTIR results were consistent with partial cleavage of ester-containing structures, while TGA and SEM revealed changes in thermal behavior and morphology. Among the tested aerogels, AAS-6 exhibited a density of approximately 0.036 g cm−3 and a porosity of 96.6%. After HDPE treatment, the aerogel exhibited a water contact angle of 135.2° while maintaining rapid oil wetting. Its 5 min liquid uptake for the tested oils and organic solvents ranged from 20.14 to 38.31 g g−1. After ten adsorption–regeneration cycles, 89–96% of the initial oil uptake was retained, depending on the oil, whereas uptake of the tested volatile solvents remained comparatively unchanged under the respective regeneration conditions. H-6 also enabled free-oil uptake from water and gravity-driven treatment of surfactant-stabilized water-in-oil (W/O) emulsions, yielding high separation efficiencies and markedly reduced dispersed-droplet signals after filtration. These results demonstrate a route for coupling the chemical conversion of cured UPR with fabrication of porous materials for oil uptake and W/O emulsion separation.

works.title: Capillary Gel Electrophoresis Separation of dsDNA Molecules Using Tetrahydroxyborate Stabilized Hydroxyethyl Cellulose – Polyvinylpyrrolidone Physical Copolymer
works.abstract: Abstract The advent of nucleic-acid–based therapeutics has revived the need to develop efficient capillary gel electrophoresis methods for their rapid, high-resolution analysis. In this paper, we introduce a dual-network hydrogel-based physical copolymer, utilizing the excellent sieving properties of hydroxyethyl cellulose with interpenetrating polyvinylpyrrolidone, which also sufficiently suppresses electroosmotic flow. Boric acid in the background electrolyte served as a cross-linker/stabilizer for the hydroxyethyl cellulose-based separation matrix via the formation of spiroborane bridges. The addition of glycerol significantly increased the resolution of separations. The excellent sieving power of the tetrahydroxyborate-stabilized HEC-PVP physical copolymer is demonstrated by the separation of dsDNA restriction fragments in a wide base pair range of 67 to 10 000, even capable of resolving identical chain length fragments. As a practical example, plasmid DNA integrity monitoring was demonstrated, facilitating the path toward a novel high-resolution separation matrix for gene therapy products in the biopharmaceuticals industry.

works.title: Removal of copper and lead ions by red mud-metakaolin based geopolymer microspheres: Insights into the efficient preparation and adsorption mechanisms
works.abstract: Abstract This study used red mud and metakaolin as the main raw material, with sodium silicate as the alkali activator. Red mud-metakaolin based geopolymer microspheres (RM-MGMs) with good sphericity and high mechanical strength are prepared via dispersion-suspension-solidification method. By investigating the adsorption performance of RM-MGMs calcined at different temperatures for Cu2+ and Pb2+, the uncalcined RM-MGMs exhibit excellent heavy metal cation adsorption due to their abundant surface hydroxyl groups and high ion exchange capacity. The optimal adsorption conditions for Cu2+/Pb2+ were adsorbent dosages of 1.5/0.3 g/L, pH of 5.3-5.6/5.0, respectively. Cu2+ adsorption reached equilibrium at 960 min. Pb2+ showed faster adsorption rate due to its smaller hydrated ionic radius and reached equilibrium at 60 min. Kinetic results indicated that the pseudo-second-order model better describes the adsorption process of RM-MGMs for Cu2+/Pb2+. Adsorption isotherm models showed that increasing temperature favors the adsorption of Cu2+/Pb2+ by RM-MGMs. At 318 K, the adsorption capacities of RM-MGMs for Cu2+/Pb2+ reach 0.86/1.43 mmol/g, respectively. In competitive experiments, the removal rates of Cu2+/Pb2+ by RM-MGMs both exceed 80%. RM-MGMs achieve adsorption of Cu2+/Pb2+ through synergistic mechanisms including ion exchange, electrostatic attraction and complexation.
